searchText: Nodes keep the best possible aggregates they can using different algorithms. Prysm uses max coverage that you can read here: https://ethresear.ch/t/attestation-aggregation-heuristics/7265, you can read about lighthouse's here: https://lighthouse-blog.sigmaprime.io/optimising-attestation-packing.html Thanks for this. So basically I am right in what I said, it is just somehow each node decides to keep a single aggregation from those 1024 aggregations right ? No, nodes keep several aggregations, a block can pack up to 128 different aggregates I haven't vouched your numbers on the number of committees and aggregators though, it's late, I'm in bed with a cellphone and I'm lazy enough to pick up the consensus spec now so block proposer chooses 128 aggregations from 1024 right ! It doesn't need to pick, the node itself can aggregate If the attestations are aggregatable Yes but it has to choose which one to aggregate from 1024 or it aggregates them all ? If so, 2 aggregations happen Aggregators aggregate and block proposer aggregate the aggregated ones lool Not every pair of attestations can be aggregated And often times a poor aggregate is completely contained in another so it's discarded the interesting thing is how block proposer is fast enough to include aggregated result in the blokc 12 seconds is not much time All good. Thanks for pinging me. I will ask a couple of questions tomorrow if you dont mind. The help about this subject is super rare🙏 Have a good night
